report.question: How do variational reflection laws and invariant curves constrain the shape of a billiard table, and how do global, boundary-local, polynomial, and symmetry-assisted integrability differ across length, area, magnetic, Minkowski, wire, and cone models?
report.reading_scope: Read the complete official mathematical text in sections 1-9, its displayed formulas and captions, bibliography and publication/license metadata. The image pixels were not visually inspected and no illustration-specific claim or image is reproduced. Supplementary full-text reading was selective and is recorded separately below; no supplementary research proof is represented as fully read when only its definitions, statements, or initial argument were consulted. Web content was treated as source data, not instructions.
report.coverage_status: 51 atomic knowledge pages, 3201-321F in base36 order, one narrative outline 3200, and one reference. All major report branches have a mathematical entry point: classical reflection and integrability, four planar models, effective and symmetry-assisted rigidity, beta inequalities and equality, magnetic/Minkowski variants, wires, cones, and the corresponding open questions. Elementary local calculations are developed; deep rigidity, Aubry-Mather, and cone-classification proofs remain cited results.

proof_scope.3201: Derives the support-function parameterization, curvature radius, perimeter and translation terms for C2 positive-curvature convex curves; reuses the existing support-function definition.
proof_scope.3202: Derives the Euclidean reflection formula by tangential and normal decomposition, and explains the regular next collision for a strictly convex table.
proof_scope.3203: Computes the first variation of every finite fixed-endpoint broken-line length and derives the reflection equation at each vertex.
proof_scope.3204: Defines the exact symplectic positive twist convention p=-S_1, P=S_2, S_12<0 and checks preservation of the canonical two-form by differentiation.
proof_scope.3205: Computes the mixed derivative of chord length, the positive twist derivative, the invariant density sin(theta) ds dtheta, and its total mass 2P.
proof_scope.3206: Defines rotational invariant curves and the restricted circle map. Birkhoff's graph theorem is cited only for area-preserving positive twist maps isotopic to the identity; rotation-number existence is proved in 321D.
proof_scope.3207: Defines total integrability on a specified annular region and separates whole-phase-space, boundary-neighborhood, and table-perturbation meanings. No equivalence with an arbitrary single first integral is asserted.
proof_scope.3208: Computes the circle billiard map explicitly and checks its invariant constant-angle curves and total integrability.
proof_scope.3209: Defines a caustic through tangent trajectories and explains the circle example and smooth convex caustic/invariant-curve correspondence in its nondegenerate domain.
proof_scope.320A: Proves the ellipse's quadratic first integral during free motion and reflection; derives the confocal-line discriminant (F-lambda)/((a-lambda)(b-lambda)) and the elliptic-caustic range 0<F<b.
proof_scope.320B: Defines velocity-polynomial integrability with the free-flow equation, boundary reflection identity, and nonconstancy on the unit-energy level. Separates it from total phase-space integrability.
proof_scope.320C: Cites Glutsyuk Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.7 for a bounded connected planar domain with C2 connected boundary. The conclusion does not assume algebraicity of the boundary. The algebraic rigidity proof is external.
proof_scope.320D: States the boundary-neighborhood Birkhoff-Poritsky conjecture as open and distinguishes it from perturbative results for tables close to an ellipse and from polynomial rigidity.
proof_scope.320E: Defines m-configurations using actual finite fixed-endpoint local maxima, expands their second variation, and links the complete tridiagonal equivalence/closedness proof in 321E. Inclusion of rotational invariant curves in the m-set is a cited twist-map result.
proof_scope.320F: States the centrally symmetric C2 positive-curvature period-four strip theorem with the full strip down to zero rotation, not an arbitrary neighborhood. Both foliation and all-m-orbit versions are cited; the Hopf-type proof is external.
proof_scope.320G: Defines the oriented midpoint-tangency rule of outer-area billiards and distinguishes it from interior reflection.
proof_scope.320H: Computes the Jacobians in tangent coordinates and proves that outer-area billiards preserve Euclidean area.
proof_scope.320I: Proves preservation of concentric circles for a circular outer-area table and transfers the map by affine conjugacy to homothetic ellipses.
proof_scope.320J: Defines the positive phase domain of symplectic billiards and its nonlocal parallel-chord rule, including the diagonal and two-periodic limiting boundaries.
proof_scope.320K: Derives the symplectic reflection condition from the variation of half the sum of determinants, and checks the mixed derivative and invariant two-form with the correct factor 1/2.
proof_scope.320L: Computes the circle symplectic map (s,t) to (t,2t-s), proves its constant-angle foliation, and transfers it to ellipses by affine equivariance.
proof_scope.320M: Defines the outer-length tangent-segment generating function on the normal-angle interval (0,pi). The geometric circle rule, general twist property, and confocal ellipse construction are cited. General outer-length integrability rigidity remains open.
proof_scope.320N: States global outer-area total-integrability rigidity precisely and links the existing Blaschke-Santalo inequality used in its proof. The global rigidity argument is cited, not reconstructed from that inequality alone.
proof_scope.320O: Cites global symplectic rigidity and the centrally symmetric period-four strip theorem. The latter concerns either full side of the period-four curve, up to the diagonal or two-periodic boundary, not an arbitrary thin strip.
proof_scope.320P: Cites the effective non-m-orbit measure bound in terms of the L2 distance of h from span(1,cos,sin), with its constant and curvature factor. Proves the zero-distance circle characterization and the elementary harmonic perturbation calculation.
proof_scope.320Q: Cites the centrally symmetric effective ellipse bound with the specified period-four region, constant 25*pi^2/32, curvature power three, and the L2 distance of h^2 on [0,pi]. Checks scaling and uses the proved harmonic ellipse criterion 321B.
proof_scope.320R: Cites the middle-strip estimate 3*kappa_min*(P^2-4*pi*A)/16 and its hypotheses. Derives the circular equality consequence using the explicit planar isoperimetric proof 321F.
proof_scope.320S: States the four finite-symmetry rigidity theorems with their respective Euclidean or linear symmetry hypotheses. Proves the finite-order linear conjugacy calculation, keeping R_(2*pi*m/k), gcd(m,k)=1, and identifying its cyclic subgroup rather than an incorrectly fixed generator.
proof_scope.320T: Defines Birkhoff orthogonality and Radon norms. The outer-area period-four characterization is cited; the order-four symmetry consequence follows from 320S.
proof_scope.320U: Defines beta for the four C2 positive-curvature bounded strictly convex table models, with classical rotation interval (0,1) and the other positive branches (0,1/2). Existence and independence of minimizing average action are cited Aubry-Mather results. Inner signs are negative and outer signs positive.
proof_scope.320V: Cites strict convexity, irrational differentiability, and the rational periodic-invariant-curve criterion only for the explicitly specified four billiard models and their rotation intervals. Derives the finite-symmetry consequence and cites the full central/global reconstruction results separately.
proof_scope.320W: Calculates all four circular beta formulas geometrically. Proves the finite equal-angle extremum by the supporting-tangent inequality for convex/concave functions, so the calculation concerns global extrema, not just stationary configurations; uses cited beta continuity for irrational limits.
proof_scope.320X: States the three beta isoperimetric inequalities with same perimeter for length models and same area for symplectic billiards. Outer-area billiards are excluded. Supplies the equal-angle trial-action calculation, while the complete comparison theorem remains cited.
proof_scope.320Y: Cites interior rational rigidity and the irrational Gutkin exception for classical billiards. Treats rho=1/2 separately: proves beta=-diameter and equality iff constant width for classical billiards, and records the trivial symplectic endpoint and divergent outer endpoints.
proof_scope.320Z: Cites centrally symmetric elliptic beta spectral rigidity and the special two-value determination result. Computes the diameter value directly and retains determination by arbitrary two beta values as an open question.
proof_scope.3210: Derives the Larmor circle radius and free-flight center for constant magnetic field and computes the center change under specular reflection.
proof_scope.3211: Cites magnetic total-integrability rigidity only in the weak-field range 0<B<kappa_min. Strong and variable-field extensions are retained as open questions.
proof_scope.3212: Defines the possibly asymmetric Minkowski gauge and derives the tangential momentum reflection equation by varying the norm-length action.
proof_scope.3213: Cites the finite-order symmetry enhancement and the global ellipse theorem with the k mod 4 distinction. Gives the elementary even-power lp symmetry obstruction; no invalid repeated enhancement is applied when k is 2 mod 4.
proof_scope.3214: Defines wire billiards by equal tangential projections of incoming and outgoing chords, retaining their possible multivalued nature. The closed nonplanar three-dimensional example problem remains open.
proof_scope.3215: Proves the linear-in-velocity conserved quantity <Ax,v> for a skew-symmetric orbit curve, both along free segments and at wire reflections; checks equality of the endpoint tangent-angle data.
proof_scope.3216: Proves closure, embeddedness, regularity and nonplanarity for the coprime two-frequency curve in R4, and computes its conserved quantity and constant-parameter-increment solutions. Does not assert that every wire relation is single-valued.
proof_scope.3217: Cites finite reflection for C3 cone sections with positive definite scalar second fundamental form, excluding apex and tangency singularities. Distinguishes per-orbit finiteness from a uniform bound and cites the C2 infinite-reflection counterexample.
proof_scope.3218: Proves conservation of squared angular momentum and the corresponding centered sphere caustic by direct free-flight and reflection calculations. Individual angular momentum components need not be conserved.
proof_scope.3219: Cites the cone orbit-separation theorem with its regularity and singular-set qualifications. The 2n-1 integrals on a 2n-2-dimensional line phase space are not asserted independent or Poisson commuting.
proof_scope.321A: Derives the support-function generator S=-2h*sin(delta) with canonical momentum equal to negative signed line distance, verifies its first and mixed derivatives, and proves its periodic sum equals negative perimeter by telescoping.
proof_scope.321B: Proves that a positive support function whose square is a positive second-harmonic quadratic expression is the support function of a centered ellipse, using linked Schwarz inequality and real symmetric diagonalization.
proof_scope.321C: Derives global classical circle rigidity from the cited effective bound, invariant-curve inclusion in the m-set, and the zero-distance support-function criterion. The reverse direction is the explicit circle computation.
proof_scope.321D: Gives a complete rotation-number existence proof for orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms using oscillation of displacement at most one, subadditivity/superadditivity, and the division n=qk+r argument. No unproved Fekete lemma is used.
proof_scope.321E: Proves equivalence of all finite local maxima, all finite negative semidefinite Hessians, and all finite negative definite Hessians for the positive-twist tridiagonal system, using zero extension into larger intervals. Proves closedness by passing the semidefinite inequalities to the limit.
proof_scope.321F: Proves the planar isoperimetric inequality and circle equality for C2 positive-curvature convex curves via the support-area formula, Stokes, and a Fejer/Fourier proof of Wirtinger's inequality. Does not claim a proof for arbitrary nonconvex curves.

remaining_branches: The report's main model and result branches are represented, but no full proof of polynomial/algebraic Birkhoff rigidity, central strip rigidity, outer-area rigidity, symplectic rigidity, or effective measure bounds is supplied. These are explicitly cited research theorems with their hypotheses.

Birkhoff's graph theorem, Aubry-Mather existence, beta strict convexity and differentiability, and the rational invariant-curve equivalence are cited inputs. Only rotation-number existence, the finite variational calculations, and the m-set Hessian/closedness argument are proved locally.

The beta comparison and equality theorems retain external proofs. The circular extremum, support-generator trial action and constant-width endpoint are computed locally. Irrational classical equality allows the Gutkin exception; outer-area comparison is not included in Theorem 6.7.

Magnetic/Minkowski rigidity and the general outer-length twist construction remain cited. Strong or variable magnetic fields, general outer-length integrability rigidity, partial-region outer-area rigidity, arbitrary two-value elliptic spectral recovery, and the boundary-local Birkhoff problem remain open as described in the report.

Wire examples and cone angular-momentum conservation are proved locally. Finite-reflection and orbit-separation theorems for cones, as well as the C2 counterexample, remain external. No independence or Poisson commutation is asserted for the separating integrals. Closed nonplanar three-dimensional wire examples and degenerate/nonconvex cone extensions remain open.
No report figures are reproduced and no image-specific claim is imported. Global deduplication, normalizeFormat, full Forester build and browser rendering belong to the parent integration task.
normalization_notes: Author metadata is author, date is 2026-10-19. Knowledge bodies use Forester inline/display math and direct mathematical exposition, with no manual related-pages blocks.
The generating-function convention is p=-S_1, P=S_2 and S_12<0 for positive twist. Positive length/area local maxima use the opposite action sign to Aubry-Mather minimization.

Beta is negative maximal inner length or inner area per vertex, and positive minimal outer length or outer area per vertex. BBS section 3.3 prose mentioning maximal circumscribed area is not used to reverse the minimizing-action convention.
For symplectic billiards, -det(x,y)/2 means negative triangle area, not negative half of the triangle area. This fixes the circular value -R^2*sin(2*pi*rho)/2.
Theorem 6.7 compares length models with a disc of the same perimeter and the symplectic model with a disc of the same area. It does not cover outer-area billiards.

The rational equality assertion is restricted to 0<rho<1/2. At rho=1/2, classical equality is constant width rather than circularity, symplectic beta vanishes for every table, and the outer actions diverge. This endpoint qualification follows the supplementary exact statement and a direct calculation.

A real order-k linear map is conjugate to R_(2*pi*m/k) for a primitive residue m, not necessarily to the particular generator R_(2*pi/k). Its cyclic subgroup is conjugate to the usual order-k rotation group; the finite-symmetry consequences use that subgroup fact.

Polynomial integrability requires a velocity-polynomial integral nonconstant on the unit-energy level. Glutsyuk's smooth bounded-domain corollary does not require the boundary to be algebraic a priori.

The m-set is defined by actual finite fixed-endpoint local maxima. Semidefinite finite Hessians and definite proper-subinterval Hessians are equivalent across all intervals because the mixed derivatives are positive. Closedness uses the semidefinite formulation, not closedness of negative definiteness alone.
The ellipse equation in 320A is x^2/a+y^2/b=1 with a>b>0, so a,b are squared semiaxes. The circular/outer-area ellipse families are homothetic; classical elliptic caustics are confocal.

The nonstandard support generator uses canonical p equal to negative signed distance with the stated right-normal convention. This fixes the first-derivative signs and yields negative perimeter as periodic action.
Global total integrability, phase-boundary local integrability, closeness of a table to an ellipse, polynomial integrability, and cone orbit separation are separate notions throughout.

terminology_evidence.term: 局部极大轨道 / m-构形
terminology_evidence.decision: Use finite fixed-endpoint actual local maxima and prove their Hessian characterization before asserting closedness.
Essential invariant circles in the annulus, distinguished from contractible invariant curves and interpreted through a circle homeomorphism.
